items.summary: Updating BrowseModePanel Range of Values for Maximum number of characters on one line Setting (#21105)
items.fullMessage:
Updating BrowseModePanel Range of Values for Maximum number of characters on one line Setting (#21105)

Closes #20478
Summary of the issue:

When browse mode is set to use screen layout navigation, paragraphs exceeding 250 characters are frequently encountered and are often split at awkward places. Increasing the limit to 1000 and adding 0 as an option will help to improve user experience.
Description of user facing changes:

Users can now set the "Maximum number of characters on one line" anywhere from 0 to 1000 characters. Selecting 0 means lines are no longer split.
Description of developer facing changes:

N/A. The change doesn't affect core logic; it is limited to changing a setting min and max values.
Description of development approach:

The setting in question is stored as config.conf["virtualBuffers"]["maxLineLength"], it is defined in source/config/configSpec.py:217 and has no min/max as indicated in source/gui/settingsDialogs.py:2615 which is where the range for the "Maximum number of characters on one line" setting is defined via a SelectOnFocusSpinCtrl. I also validated that logic in nvdaHelper/vbufBase/storage.cpp:1074-1210 only takes maxLength into consideration if it is larger than 0. I leveraged AI to understand the flow of code from setting the value in the Browse Mode Panel to the line splitting portion of the code to ensure that adding the new range did not break existing code. I also used AI to create unit tests and system tests replicating the behavior I tested manually.
